fixes.explanation: You got it, baker. Shem, Ham and Japheth are the three, and from them the whole earth was populated. Three brothers, and a whole earth full of people came from them. I once stamped one batch and thought MY arms were tired.

A city is too small, friend. The verse says these three were the sons of Noah, and from them the whole earth was populated. That's the whole earth, not one city. Picture one family photo that keeps needing a bigger wall.

Yes, a vineyard. Noah, a man of the soil, proceeds to plant one, and the text goes on to say he drank some of its wine. Soil work, then vines, then wine, all in two verses. That's the order the text gives us.
I see why that one tempts you. An olive grove is a fine thing to plant, but it isn't what this verse says. Noah planted a vineyard, and the very next verse mentions its wine.

True. Noah says, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem!" and then, "May Canaan be the servant of Shem." The two sentences come back to back. Verse 27 goes on to say, "may Canaan be his servant," and the text doesn't spell out whose servant that is.

It's true, friend, and here's what the text says. Noah declares, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem!" and in the same breath, "May Canaan be the servant of Shem." So Canaan is named as Shem's servant right after the blessing. Verse 27 then says, "may Canaan be his servant," and it leaves open whose servant that is.

Yes. Noah says, "May God expand the territory of Japheth…" That's a wish for more room, and the words are "may God," so it's what Noah asks for. Every cookie sheet in my bakery is full, so I understand wishing for more space.
